name: The Glaucous Lull

detectability.signature: A glaucous-toned silence: gravimetric returns flatline and stellar parallax reads wrong, marking a region where nothing pulls at anything.

proximity: Inertial reference frames fail, leaving autopilots effectively blind
Stellar parallax shifts subtly, giving navigators the sensation of falling upward
contact: Vessels coast helplessly at constant velocity, unable to turn or brake
Loose objects and crew float in perfect weightlessness as the ship loses all gravitational footing
prolonged_exposure: Crews report dissociation and vertigo from weeks without any felt gravity
Ships without pre-planned momentum budgets drift out the far side on random vectors, permanently lost

phenomena: Navigation instruments giving contradictory readings across the boundary
Objects moving in perfectly straight, thrustless lines inside
Absence of gravitational lensing precisely where lensing should occur
hazards: Navigation system failure and unrecoverable course loss
Structural collapse from unbalanced stresses when re-entering real gravity gradients
opportunities: Natural defensive position, as pursuing fleets cannot maneuver inside
Unique research opportunity into the texture of spacetime itself
Smuggling route for vessels willing to coast ballistic and silent
known_incidents: The frigate Ninefold Gate entered in 2296 on routine patrol and exited eleven months later, stern-first, four light-months off station.
Salvage guilds mark the Lull's western margin with warning buoys; the buoys are found, each season, somewhere new.
description: Nothing marks the Glaucous Lull but a wrongness in the stars, a faint grey-blue flattening of depth where parallax refuses to agree with itself. There is no glow, no ring, no shadow; only the absence of pull. Instruments cross the border and begin politely contradicting one another.

Inside, gravity simply does not happen. Debris hangs in crisp suspension, and vessels keep whatever velocity they carried across the threshold, coasting in straight lines toward arbitrary fates. The whole region wanders erratically through the sector, its ragged border redrawn by no clock anyone has found.

The void was named by the patrol frigate Ninefold Gate, which entered on a routine sweep in 2296 and drifted out eleven months later, stern-first, four light-months from its beat. Cartographers have mapped six borders for it; every one has been wrong within a year. Physicists argue whether it is a wound in spacetime or spacetime's default state briefly remembered.

Smugglers prize the Lull because pursuers cannot chase what cannot turn, and war colleges teach it as the sector's largest trap. Survey drones seeded along its margins transmit until they, too, go quiet and straight. Wise captains give the grey-blue stillness a wide berth and let it drift where it will.
